title: Contextual SLO orchestration and anomaly harmonization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Unify tracing hooks, metrics/log pipelines, and latency/error dashboards into a single SLO orchestration layer that reduces noisy paging and improves signal fidelity. This ticket implements a telemetry gateway that enriches incoming traces with runtime context (route, model, customer tier), normalizes metrics and logs in the ingestion pipeline, and deploys an "anomaly harmonizer" service that fuses trace/metric/log signals into a single anomaly score used by burn-rate and paging policies. The goal is to enable contextual alerting (route- and model-aware), dynamic quiet windows for low-impact regressions, and correlation hints in the console dashboards for faster triage.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry gateway deployed to staging and tags traces with route/model/customer_tier and request_id
Metrics/log normalization pipeline implemented and validated on a 48h replay of prod ingest (no schema drift >0.5%)
Anomaly harmonizer prototype running in staging scoring combined signals and exposing an API consumed by alerting rules
Paging noise reduced by >=30% on sampled routes (compare last 30 days baseline to first 14 days post-deploy)
New SLO orchestration dashboard available in Grafana with trace-to-alert drilldowns and a table of suppressed vs fired burn-rate alerts
Integration tests and runbook updates added to docs; incident playbook includes escalation thresholds and fallback policies
updates: 2026-03-11 — Spike completed: validated approach for injecting route/model context at runtime hooks; demoed to Observability guild (notes: confluence/redwood/tel-gateway-spike)

2026-03-12 — PoC anomaly harmonizer implemented (python prototype + kafka consumer). Early results show better grouping of error bursts across models; opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/412

2026-03-13 — Benchmarked enrichment overhead: median latency increase per request is 6ms at 50th percentile, 18ms at 99th percentile when enrichment cache miss occurs; added local caching to reduce tail latency
2026-03-14 — Drafted alerting playbook and dynamic quiet window algorithm; solicited feedback from SRE and Product on acceptable suppression policies
decisions: Use existing Kafka ingestion path and add a Flink streaming job for normalization and enrichment to avoid duplicating ingestion code
Anomaly harmonizer will use an ensemble scoring model (rules + lightweight statistical detectors) rather than a heavy ML model to keep compute predictable
SLOs will be evaluated per (route, model, customer_tier) tuple and aggregated upwards for team-level dashboards
Burn-rate alerts will be gated behind an anomaly score threshold and a secondary impact check (requests/sec and error-volume percentile) to reduce false positives
blockers: High cardinality of model tags causing cardinality explosion in metrics backend — need tag bucketing strategy
Security review for the telemetry gateway (intercepts/annotates request metadata) is pending compliance approval
Capacity planning for Flink jobs — need to size cluster to handle enrichment for peak ingest rates
risks: If enrichment adds too much tail latency, downstream route SLIs may be impacted — mitigation: hop-by-hop sampling and async enrichment fallback
Incorrect normalization buckets may hide regressions for minority customers — mitigation: preserve raw telemetry stream for replay and audit
Operator confusion from merged anomaly signals — mitigation: surface signal provenance and confidence in dashboards
next_steps: Land telemetry gateway sidecar change in runtime to add route/model context (PR opened)
Deploy Flink normalization job to staging and run 48h ingest replay; validate schema and cardinality metrics
Hard-stop for production rollout: finish compliance/security review and add e2e test that verifies alert suppression behavior
Iterate on playbook thresholds with SRE over next 2 week cycle and run simulated incident drill
